fixes.explanation: That's it. “…because of his oaths and his guests, he did not want to refuse her.” (Mark 6:26) He had sworn in front of the leading men of Galilee (Mark 6:21-23). I think that's a sad thing to be stuck on, a promise made too fast.

That's right, baker. “When John’s disciples heard about this, they came and took his body and placed it in a tomb.” (Mark 6:29) After all that darkness, there are people who came to care for him. I think that's a quiet, faithful thing, and I'm glad Mark tells us.

Samuel, the prophet who anointed Saul as king (1 Samuel 10:1), doesn't come up in this passage. The people say, “John the Baptist has risen from the dead!” (Mark 6:14) That's the name in the rumor. Good guess for a prophet, though, because the crowd was guessing prophets all over the place.

Cousin doesn't show up in this verse. The text says “…his brother Philip’s wife Herodias, whom Herod had married.” (Mark 6:17) So Philip is Herod's brother. Close family, friend, and John says plainly, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife!” (Mark 6:18)

That's right. John said, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife!” (Mark 6:18) Herodias did not shrug it off. She held a grudge and wanted to kill him (Mark 6:19). Some people let a thing go, and some people hold it tight.

True. Mark 6:20 says that when Herod heard John's words, “…he was greatly perplexed; yet he listened to him gladly.” Confused and still listening gladly. I know that feeling, like the time I read a recipe three times and still wasn't sure.
Not quite. The text says, “At once the girl hurried back to the king…” (Mark 6:25) No long wait is mentioned. She went back right away with her request.

Right. She did not take her time. “At once the girl hurried back to the king with her request…” (Mark 6:25) She even asked for it “immediately.” It's a heavy part of the story, friend, and the text shows how fast it moved.
